item.title: Collision of two trains in Egypt kills at least four
item.description: President orders prompt investigation after one train derails in collision in al-Ayyat about 30 miles from Cairo At least four people were killed and almost 90 others were injured when two trains collided on Sunday south of the Egyptian capital, Cairo, authorities have said. The crash occurred in al-Ayyat district in Giza province, about 30 miles south of Cairo, when a train travelling to the south-western Fayoum province crashed into the rear of a train heading to the southern province of Aswan, according to the transportation ministry. It said one of the trains derailed. Continue reading... Fuente: The Guardian - World.

item.title: Louisiana court backs homeowner's right to block neighbours from private road beyond 1,000 feet
item.description: Mona Matherne spent over a decade contesting neighbors' use of a private road beside her country home. In November 2026, state appeals judges upheld her property rights and confirmed previous court orders. Matherne successfully argued against her neighbors, who claimed the road was public. The court ruled that only the first 1,000 feet was public, protecting Matherne's privacy. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

Scillonian III, also known as the “vomit comet” because in stormy weather it tended to rock a little too much for the comfort of those susceptible to sea sickness, has chugged between the British mainland and the Isles of Scilly, for just shy of half a century.
